title: Polynomial-Time Adjacency Encoding
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $n,s,o$ assign a natural number to each Boolean string. Suppose the functions $x\mapsto 1^{n(x)}$, $x\mapsto 1^{s(x)}$, and $x\mapsto 1^{o(x)}$ are each computable in polynomial time by finite-state Turing machines. Then the function mapping $x$ to the serialized CNF obtained from the adjacency constraints for parameters $n(x),s(x)$ by shifting every variable index by $o(x)$ is computable in polynomial time.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let
$n,s,o:\{0,1	ext{-strings}	o\mathbb N\}$ be functions such that each of the three maps
$x\mapsto 1^{n(x)}$, $x\mapsto 1^{s(x)}$, and $x\mapsto 1^{o(x)}$ is computable in
polynomial time in the stated machine model. Then the map sending $x$ to the binary
encoding of the adjacency CNF for parameters $n(x),s(x)$, with every variable index
shifted by $o(x)$, is polynomial-time computable.
